title: The canary confirms the exact model is available and names a permitted auth source
statement: Before a provider contract is accepted, a disposable restricted child using the pinned Pi SDK resolves the exact selected provider and model. Availability comes from that exact model appearing in the available-model set, never merely from the provider reporting configured. A successful report contains only provider, model, availability and an auth-source category permitted by the declared contract. Planted credentials, variable names, headers and credential-derived fingerprints appear in no report, refusal, stdout or stderr, against a positive control. All disposable state is confined to a temporary root removed on success and refusal.
notes: ⚠️ AVAILABILITY AND `configured` DISAGREE, AND THE DISAGREEMENT IS MEASURED. The pinned runtime's `getProviderAuthStatus()` can report `configured: true` while `hasConfiguredAuth()` is false and the model is absent from `getAvailable()`; the compatibility spike's `withOAuth` cell records exactly that, with `statusDisagreesWithAvailability: true`. Anything gating on "some authentication source is configured" tells an operator they are connected when they cannot infer, which is why this criterion names the available-model set rather than the status object. ⚠️ THE PERMITTED CATEGORIES ARE THE THREE CMP-0029 DECLARES. Pi's own vocabulary is wider: `runtime` means a key was passed on the command line, and `models_json_command` and `fallback` are routes that produce a credential by executing something or by inheriting an extension's. None of the three is a category Kiln permits, so each is a refusal rather than a classification — mapping them onto `custom-environment-key` would let a route the table refuses arrive under a name it accepts. ⚠️ THE REPORT IS A CLOSED SHAPE, NOT A FILTERED ONE. Pi's `environment` status carries a `label` built from `getConfigValueEnvVarNames()` — variable NAMES — so a report assembled by spreading the status object leaks them by default. Asserting the absence of known-bad fields cannot see a field nobody thought of; asserting the exact key set can. ⚠️ WHAT THIS CANNOT REACH, and it is an evidence omission rather than a gap in the criterion: OAuth for a BUILT-IN provider needs an interactive `/login` against a real account. A `models.json` provider is composed with apiKey auth only, so a stored OAuth credential for one has no flow to resolve it — the spike records this as `oauthProvedForCustomProvider: false` and `oauthRemainsOpenForBuiltInProviders: true`. Real completions, token refresh and subscription-tier behaviour are account-bound for the same reason.
